judged_text: SalesforceCalendarService now performs an unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a prisma.credential.update on every service construction — no expiry/isExpired guard, and no routing through refreshOAuthTokens — creating a parallel refresh path that duplicates jsforce's own OAuth refresh and bypasses the sync abstraction every other app in this PR uses. Every availability check and booking involving a Salesforce-connected user now makes a login.salesforce.com round trip (which counts against the org's Salesforce API/login limits) plus a DB write, even on hosts that never enable credential sharing: hot-path latency and org API-quota exhaustion are added to all Salesforce booking flows, and concurrent constructions race read-modify-write on credential.key.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now unconditionally performs a token refresh request (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)`) and then immediately writes the refreshed token into the DB (`await prisma.credential.update(...)`) before constructing the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no expiry/"isExpired"-style guard shown, so this refresh+DB-write happens whenever this code path runs, and it also does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens` abstraction used elsewhere in the PR. The added network call and write on what is likely a hot path is a concrete behavior change visible in the diff.
